text:
maya: Pushing a canary (runtime@r3a8) to the eu-west pool. Heads up: this includes the new kernel-selection and KV eviction tweaks.
aj: Noticed canary nodes with steadily increasing RSS on long-seq workloads, p95 latency also bumped.
liam: Can you share numbers? I ran a short load and saw fragmentation climb after ~2000 requests.
maya: Roughs: avg RSS +22% vs baseline, memory alloc spikes around token 1024 boundary.
sophie: perf-bot just posted a CI alert: `perf/regression: p95+18%` and `mem-leak:true` flags.
perf-bot: nightly-run: model-ci/large-seq test failed. Trigger: memory-pressure threshold exceeded.
aj: This smells like KV cache churn — eviction window was changed to favor smaller windows in the batching heuristic PR. Could be more misses + mem churn.
liam: I profiled the canary with heaptrack quickly. Allocation buckets show lots of small allocations from kv_cache::Shard::evict_range.
maya: Paste from the heaptrace snippet:
```
kv_cache::Shard::insert -> allocate(32k) x N
kv_cache::Shard::evict_range -> free partial, leave fragmentation
Allocator::split_chunk: 8k fragments
```
aj: That matches: eviction now evicts contiguous pages by recent-LRU ranges which can leave tiny leftover fragments; combined with our custom jemalloc settings it's bad.
sophie: Any idea which merge introduced the eviction semantics change?
liam: bisect points to PR #4829 (batching+eviction heuristics). Reverting that locally on canary removes the mem-growth.
maya: I just triggered a revert of PR #4829 on canary. Monitoring.
deploy-bot: revert PR#4829 applied to canary cluster (eu-west).
oncall: Alert: one canary hit OOM at 1749506820; container restarted.
aj: OOM happened exactly when a sequence > 1500 tokens arrived. Sequence-length sensitivity seems real.
liam: Quick experiment: force using old kernel selection (legacy-kernel) and keep new batching — memory stays stable. So two interacting changes: kernel selection + eviction heuristics.
sophie: So rollout is blocked until we untangle. I'll mark the stable rollout as blocked in the release tracker.
maya: Agree. Steps: 1) keep PR #4829 reverted on canary, 2) add allocation guardrails in KV cache (cap frag growth), 3) add CI test with variable-length sequences to catch regressions.
aj: Also add perf regression gate for mem fragmentation metric in CI. The current perf tests only check p50/p95 but not fragmentation.
liam: I'll open a small PR to add a microbench that simulates mixed sequence lengths and asserts no steady RSS growth after N iterations.
maya: For now, rolling back canary to baseline. Anyone object?
sophie: No objections. Blocker status: release blocked until root cause fixed and tests added.
perf-bot: created issue perf/fragmentation-4829 and linked failing CI artifacts.
aj: FYI, repro script in /eng-runtime/tools/repro_kv_fragment.sh (local only) — will push to the repo with instructions.
maya: Thanks. Let's sync in the 10-min incident triage.
liam: Will include perf maps and jemalloc stats in the triage notes.
sophie: Adding action items to the release channel. :warning:
